newsitem.title: USA: IPO FOCUS - Staffmark due in rough time for industry.
newsitem.headline: IPO FOCUS - Staffmark due in rough time for industry.

text.p: StaffMark Inc's initial public offering Thursday should garner premiums despite its limited operating history and recent industry troubles, as investors bet the IPO could be a bargain way to invest in the the temporary staffing industry.
"The stock should do well. It's on our our hot list, although we'll have to see if it can get past the downward revision," said IPO Financial Network president David Menlow.
StaffMark plans to offer 5.5 million shares for between $9 and $11 each, revised down a notch from its initial estimated pricing range of $10 to $12.

Recent IPOs of "temp" firms have provided smashing returns. All three temp firms that went public this summer have seen their stock climb steadily over the past few months to 30 percent or more above their IPO price.
The cream of the crop, RemedyTemp Inc, has risen about 45 percent from its July IPO price of $13 to around $19. Source Services Corp, and Professional Staff Inc have both risen about 30 percent.
But StaffMark's IPO may have just missed the boat.

Last week, industry leader Manpower Inc guided down analysts' 1996 earnings estimates, sending its stock below support levels. Other temp companies fell, including Olsten Corp, Kelly Services, RemedyTemp and Source Services.
"We may have to see how far along the route the train has traveled with this sector. Guess? Inc should have done well, but its IPO came out too late; it could be the same type of thing," Menlow said.
Clothing firm Guess, which was expected to perform well, has slipped from its August IPO price of $18 to trade at about $15.
William Sutherland, analyst for Janney Montgomery Scott, said the temporary industry, although its growth rates are declining slightly, is hardly in dire straits.

"It has become more difficult to find qualified permanent people, so the agencies have been able to raise prices in line with or ahead of underlying wage prices. So gross margins are in good shape," he said.

According to the National Association of Temporary Staffing Services, the U.S. market for temporary staffing services has grown at a compound annual rate of 17.7 percent from $20.4 billion in 1991 revenue to $39.2 billion in 1995.
Sutherland said overall growth has slowed somewhat in the core temporary staffing services but has been boosted by strong growth in specialty areas such as information technologies.
"Without the growth in the specialty areas, (growth) would probably be in the low teens," he said. "And I think it will slow a bit next year as comparisons get tougher."

StaffMark was founded only five months ago to provide staffing services in the southeastern and southwestern United States. At the close of the deal, it will buy six "founding" companies, according to the prospectus. Together, they provide more than 10,000 employees to over 2,500 clients weekly.

StaffMark plans to use $15.9 million of the gross proceeds of about $55 million to buy the six firms. This has raised red flags in the minds of some analysts. The IPO Insider has the deal on its "Not Recommended" list, citing the use of proceeds and other circumstances.
The IPO is tentatively slated for Thursday.
